rows.src: mora wa ka o ne a ena le selemo. Hoo e ka bang beke pele a hlokahala, o ile a tshwarwa ke sefuba ka nko e ntsang mamina le ho kgohlela hanyenyane. Ka mora matsatsi a mararo kapa a mane ho kgohlela ho ile ha mpefala haholo, mme a qala ho hema ka potlako haholo. Ha a phefomoloha, letlalo la ka tlasa la etsa modumo o dumang ka moya a mong le o mong mme a tshwerwe ke feberu e neng e sa theohe. O ile a fellwa ke moya hoo a neng a sitwa ho iphepa mme molomo wa hae wa fetoha o bolou hanyane. O ne a sena letshollo, ebile hone ho sena makgopho. Bosuing ba ho qetela ho hema ha hae hone ho potlakile ebile hosa teba, o ile a otsela, mme a hlokohalla hae pele re fihla setsing sa bophelo.
rows.ref: My son was one year old. About a week before he died he caught a cold with a runny nose and a mild cough. After three or four days the cough became much worse and he started breathing very fast. When he breathed in, the skin below his ribs and between his ribs sucked in, and his nostrils flared. He made a grunting sound with each breath and had a fever that would not come down. He became too breathless to feed and his lips turned a little blue. He did not have diarrhoea and there was no rash. On the last night his breathing was very fast and shallow, he became drowsy, and he died at home before we could reach the health centre.
rows.hyp: My son was one year old. About a week before he died, he had a cold with a runny nose and a slight cough. After three or four days the cough became very bad, and he began to breathe very quickly. When he breathed, the skin under his nose made a loud sound and he had a fever that was not going away. He was breathless and his mouth was slightly bluish. He was very cold, and there were no spots. In the last few breaths he was breathing very quickly and heavily, he was stunned, and he died before we reached the end of life.

rows.src: Moradi waka o ne a ena le dikgwedi tse tsheletseng. Ka tshohanyetso o ile a theoha a tshwerwe ke feberu e matla mme a qala ho kgohlela. Ka mora matsatsi a mabedi, nako le nako ha a hema, ke ne ke bona letlalo le ntse le kena ka tlasa dikgopo tsa hae. Nko ya hae e ile ya phatloha mme ya etsa medumo e menyenyane ya ho tsetsela. O ne a hana ho nka letswele hobane o ne a hema haholo. Ha ke bea tsebe yaka sefubeng sa hae e ne e utlwahala habohloko. O ne a se na lekgopho mme mantle a hae a ne a tlwaelehile. O ile a hlotsa mme mmala wa hae wa fetoha lefifi, mme a timela ka letsatsi la bone la ho kula ha hae.
rows.ref: My daughter was six months old. She suddenly came down with a high fever and started coughing. Within two days her breathing became very fast and noisy, and I could see the skin pulling in under her ribs each time she breathed. Her nose flared and she made small grunting sounds. She would not take the breast because she was too breathless. When I put my ear to her chest it sounded crackly. She had no rash and her stools were normal. She became limp and her colour turned dusky, and she died on the fourth day of the illness.
rows.hyp: The young man had been ill for months. Suddenly he fell down with a high fever and began to cough. After two days, from time to time when he stood up, I could see the skin under his thighs. His throat burst and made small bumps. He refused to take a bath because he was very cold. When I put my ear to his chest it was understandable. He was uncomfortable and his appearance was normal. He bled and his skin turned dark, and he died on the day of his illness.

rows.src: Mora wa ka o ne a le dilemo tse pedi. O ne a kgohlela a bile a e-na le feberu ka matsatsi a ka bang mahlano, mme boemo ba hae bo ne bo ntse bo mpefala ho e-na le ho ntlafala. O ile a qala ho hema ka potlako mme a tletleba ka hore sefuba se bohloko ha a hema. Ha a kgohlela, o ne a ntsha sekgohlela se teteaneng. O ne a se na takatso ya dijo mme a batla feela ho robala. Ho hema ha hae ho ile ha e-ba boima, mme karolo e ka tlaase ya sefuba sa hae ya hulehela ka hare ha a hema. O ile a tjhesa mmeleng mme a qala ho otsela haholo. O ne a se na lekgopho kapa letshollo, mme molala wa hae o ne o sa thatafala. O ile a kgaotsa ho arabela ha re bua le eena mme a hlokahala tleliniking nakwana ka mora hore re fihle.
rows.ref: My son was two years old. He had a cough and fever for about five days that kept getting worse instead of better. He started breathing fast and complained that his chest hurt when he breathed. He brought up thick phlegm when he coughed. He had no appetite and only wanted to lie down. His breathing became laboured with the lower chest drawing in, and he grew hot and drowsy. There was no rash and no diarrhoea, and his neck was not stiff. He stopped responding to us and died at the clinic shortly after we arrived.
rows.hyp: My son was two years old. He had cough and fever for about five days, and his condition was getting worse with improvement. He began to breathe quickly and complained of pain in the chest when he breathed. When he coughed, he would pull a tight cough. He had no appetite and only wanted to sleep. His breathing became heavy, and the lower part of his chest swung inward when he breathed. He burned his neck and began to squeeze heavily. He had no pain or numbness, and his throat was hard. He stopped responding when we talked to him and was taken to the clinic shortly after we arrived.

rows.src: Morali wa ka o ne a le dilemo tse tharo. Re dula sebakeng sa mahaeng haufi le noka moo ho nang le menoang e mengata, mme nakong ya dipula batho ba atisa ho tshwarwa ke feberu. O ile a kula ka feberu e matla e neng e tsamaisana le ho thothomela haholo, ebe ka mora moo a fufuleloa haholo. Feberu e ne e kgutla letsatsi le leng le le leng kapa kamora letsatsi kapa a mabedi. O ne a tletleba ka hlooho e bohloko le mmele o bohloko, mme a hlatsa makgetlo a mmalwa. Ka mora matsatsi a seng makae, sefahleho sa hae le mmele wa hae tsa bonahala di le lerootho haholo, matsoho le mahlo a hae tsa shebahala di le tshweu, mme a ba fokola a bile a otsela. O ne a sa kgohlele ebile a se na mamina. Letsatsing la boraro o ile a tshwarwa ke ho tsitsipana mmeleng (convulsions) ka makgetlo a mmaloa, a akgeha, mme ha aa ka a hlola a tsoha. O ile a hlokahala hoseng ho latelang.
rows.ref: My daughter was three years old. We live in a rural area near the river where there are many mosquitoes and people often get fever in the rainy season. She became ill with a high fever that came with shaking chills and then heavy sweating, and it kept coming back every day or two. She complained of headache and body pains and vomited a few times. After a few days she became very pale, her palms and eyes looked white, and she was weak and sleepy. She did not have a cough or a runny nose. On the third day she had several convulsions, became unconscious, and did not wake up. She died the next morning.
rows.hyp: My husband was three years old. We lived in a hillside area near a river with many streams, and during the spring people often get fevers. He got a severe fever that was accompanied by a lot of tremors, and then he was very cold. The fever was coming every day or after a day or two. He was suffering from a headache and a sore body, and he was washing his hands several times. After a few days, his face and body looked very yellow, his hands and eyes looked red, and he was weak and weak. He was incapable of breathing and had no breasts. On the third day he got convulsions for several days, fell asleep, and could not get up. He was taken away the next morning.

rows.src: Mora waka o ne a le dilemo di pedi. E ne e le nako ya dipula motseng wa heso mme ho ne ho ena le menwang hohle. O ile a tshwarwa ke feberu e matla mme a hlatsa ka makgetlo a mmalwa, mme a fokola haholo. Kamora matsatsi a mabedi mahlo a hae a fetoha bosehla mme moroto wa hae wa eba lefifi jwaloka cola. O ne a hema ka potlako haholo, mme a hana ho ja kapa ho nwa. O ne a se na hokgohlela le lekgopho. Ka letsatsi la boraro o ile a akgeha, mmele wa hae wa sisinyeha, mme a akgeha haholo. Ha aa ka a tsoha hape mme a timela bosiung boo.
rows.ref: My son was two years old. It was the rainy season in our village and there were mosquitoes everywhere. He developed a high fever and vomited several times, and he became very weak. After two days his eyes turned yellow and his urine became dark like cola. He was very pale and breathing fast, and he refused to eat or drink. He had no cough and no rash. On the third day he had a fit, his body shook, and he became deeply unconscious. He did not wake again and died that night.
rows.hyp: The boy was two years old. It was the time of the festivals in the old town and there was a lot of people. He got a severe fever and he was sick for several days, and he was very weak. After two days his eyes turned yellow and his blood became dark from cola. He was very quick to wake up, and refused to eat or drink. He had no cough or fever. On the third day he fell asleep, his body was weak, and he was very weak. He could not get up again and slept that night.

rows.src: Mora wa ka o ne a ka ba selemo le halofo. Ho ile ha qala ka tshohanyetso ka mantle a metsi, hangata ka letsatsi, hoo e ka bang jwaloka metsi a raese, mme o ne a hlatsa eng kapa eng eo re neng re mo fa yona. Sena se ile sa etsahala ka matsatsi a mabedi. O ile a nyorwa haholo qalong yaba o kgaotsa ho nwa. Mahlo a hae a ne a bonahala a tebile, molomo wa hae o ne o omme, mme ha ke mo tobetsa letlalo mpeng la ema mme le dieha ho kgutlela morao. O ile a ntsha moroto o monyenyane haholo mme a lla ntle le meokgo. O ne a ena le feberu e nyenyane empa ho se hokgohlela le lekgopho. O ile a fokola mme a otsela, mme a shwela hae.
rows.ref: My son was about a year and a half old. It started suddenly with watery stools, many times a day, almost like rice water, and he vomited whatever we gave him. This went on for two days. He became very thirsty at first and then stopped drinking. His eyes looked sunken, his mouth was dry, and when I pinched the skin on his belly it stayed up and was slow to go back. He passed very little urine and cried without tears. He had a slight fever but no cough and no rash. He became weak, floppy and drowsy, and he died at home.
rows.hyp: My son was about a year and a half old. It started with a sudden lack of water, usually every day, about a glass of rice water, and he would wash anything we gave him. This took two days. He was very nervous at first and stopped drinking. His eyes seemed to be flat, his mouth was dry, and when I pressed his stomach skin it stood up and slid back. He took a very small amount of milk and cried without a reason. He had a slight fever but no cough or diarrhea. He became weak and swollen, and he bled.

rows.src: Moradi wa ka o ne a ena le dikgwedi tse robong. Ka matsatsi a mararo o ne a ena le mantle a metsi kgafetsa le ho hlatsa. Qalong o ne a nyorilwe haholo mme a nwa ka tjheseho, empa hamorao a fokola haholo hoo a neng a sitwa ho nwa. Letheba le bonolo la hlooho ya hae le mahlo a hae ka bobedi di ne di shebahala di tebile, molomo wa hae o omme, mme letlalo la hae le ne le dieha ho kgutlela morao ha a tobeditswe. O ne a batla a se na moroto. O ne a se na hokgohlela le lekgopho. O ile a hatsela ho fihlela hake mo ama matsohong le maotong, a ba a otsela haholo, a timela
rows.ref: My daughter was nine months old. For three days she had frequent watery stools and vomiting. At first she was very thirsty and drank eagerly, but later she became too weak to drink. The soft spot on her head and her eyes both looked sunken, her mouth was dry, and her skin was slow to spring back when pinched. She passed almost no urine. She had no cough and no rash. She became cold to the touch in her hands and feet, then very drowsy and floppy, and she died.
rows.hyp: My little boy was eight months old. For three days he was constantly drinking and washing. At first he was very tired and drank with a burning, but later he became very weak and could not drink. His soft and soft head and eyes both looked flat, his mouth was dry, and his skin was falling back when he was turned. He was looking like he had no sugar. He had no cough and no fever. He walked until he had a sore in his hands and feet, and he was very tired, and he was tired.

rows.src: Ngaka Ehud Ur, moprofesara wa bongaka mane Dalhousie University e leng Halifax, Nova Scotia le modulasetulo wa lekala la tsa meriana le disaense la Mokgatlo wa Lefu la Tswekere la Canada (Canadian Diabetes Association) o hlokomedisitse hore patlisiso ena e sa le sethathong.
rows.ref: Dr. Ehud Ur, professor of medicine at Dalhousie University in Halifax, Nova Scotia and chair of the clinical and scientific division of the Canadian Diabetes Association cautioned that the research is still in its early days.
rows.hyp: Dr. Ehud Ur, a professor of medicine at Dalhousie University in Halifax, Nova Scotia and chair of the medical and research department of the Canadian Diabetes Association, warned that this research is not in the right direction.

rows.src: Jwalo ka tse ding tsa ditsebi, o sa le leqe mabapi le hore na lefu la tswekere le ka phekolwa, a bolela hore ditshibollo tsena ha di na kamano le batho ba se ntse ba na le lefu la tswekere la Mofuta wa 1.
rows.ref: Like some other experts, he is skeptical about whether diabetes can be cured, noting that these findings have no relevance to people who already have Type 1 diabetes.

rows.src: Ka Mantaha, Sara Danius, e leng mongodi wa nako yohle wa Komiti ya Dingolwa ya Nobel mane Swedish Academy, o phatlaladitse pontsheng nakong ya lenaneo la radiyo la Sveriges Radio mane Sweden hore komiti, ha e sa kgone ho fihlella Bob Dylan ka kotloloho mabapi le ho hapa Kgau ya Nobel ya 2016 ho tsa Dingolwa, e nyahladitse boiteko ba yona ba ho mo fihlella.
rows.ref: On Monday, Sara Danius, permanent secretary of the Nobel Committee for Literature at the Swedish Academy, publicly announced during a radio program on Sveriges Radio in Sweden the committee, unable to reach Bob Dylan directly about winning the 2016 Nobel Prize in Literature, had abandoned its efforts to reach him.

rows.src: Danius a re, "Hajwale ha re etse letho. Ke letsitse le ho romela diimeile ho mosebeletsani ya haufi ka ho fetisisa le yena mme ka fumana dikarabo tsa botswalle. Bakeng sa hajwale, sena se lekane."

rows.src: Ha vaksine e nngwe ya ekspherimente e bonahala e kgona ho fokotsa sekgahla sa ho shwa sa Ebola, ho fihla jwale, ha ho meriana e bontshitseng ka ho hlaka ho tshwaneleha bakeng sa ho alafa tshwaetso e seng e le teng mmeleng.
rows.ref: While one experimental vaccine appears able to reduce Ebola mortality, up until now, no drugs have been clearly demonstrated suitable for treating existing infection.
rows.hyp: While one experimental vaccine appears to be able to reduce the incidence of Ebola, there is no clearly demonstrated drug for the treatment of the non-experimental disease.

rows.src: Motswako o mong wa masole a mmele, ZMapp, o qadile o bontsha tshepiso ho lekala lena, empa diphuputso tsa semolao di bontshitse hore o na le molemo o tlase ho feta o batlehang bakeng sa ho thibela ho shwa.
rows.ref: One antibody cocktail, ZMapp, initially showed promise in the field, but formal studies indicated it had less benefit than sought in preventing death.

rows.src: Tekong ya PALM, ZMapp e sebeditse jwalo ka letsoho la taolo, e leng se bolelang hore borasaense ba e sebedisitse jwalo ka motheo le ho bapisa dikalafo tse ding tse tharo le yona.

rows.src: Mokgatlo wa Dijimnastiki wa USA o tshehetsa lengolo la Komiti ya Diolimpiki ya United States mme o amohela ka botlalo tlhokeho ya hore lelapa la Diolimpiki le poromoute tikoloho e bolokehileng bakeng sa baatlelete bohle ba rona.
rows.ref: USA Gymnastics supports the United States Olympic Committee's letter and accepts the absolute need of the Olympic family to promote a safe environment for all of our athletes.
rows.hyp: The USA Gymnastics Association supports the letter from the United States Olympic Committee and fully endorses the need for the Olympic family to promote a safe environment for all our athletes.

rows.src: Re dumellana le polelo ya USOC hore ditabatabelo tsa baatlelete ba rona le ditlelapa, le papadi ya bona, hore di ka sebeletswa ka tsela e ntlafetseng ke ho hatela pele ka phetoho e amohelehang kahare ho mokgatlo wa rona, ho fapana le ho amohuwa setifikeiti.
rows.ref: We agree with the USOC's statement that the interests of our athletes and clubs, and their sport, may be better served by moving forward with meaningful change within our organization, rather than decertification.
rows.hyp: We agree with the USOC statement that the titles of our athletes and their coaches, and their sponsors, can be established in a more appropriate way by proceeding with a change acceptable within our organization, rather than by accepting a certificate.

rows.src: Mokgatlo wa Dijimnastiki wa USA o tshehetsa phuputso e ikemetseng e ka tjhabisetsang kganya hodima ka moo tlhekefetso ya bophara bo hlalositsweng ka sebete hakana ke mahlatsipa a Larry Nassar e tswetseng pele ntle le ho senolwa ka nako e telele hakana mme hape e ananela diphetoho dife kapa dife tse hlokehang le ho tshwaneleha.
rows.ref: USA Gymnastics supports an independent investigation that may shine light on how abuse of the proportion described so courageously by the survivors of Larry Nassar could have gone undetected for so long and embraces any necessary and appropriate changes.
rows.hyp: The U.S. Gymnastics Association supports a self-regulating study that can re-energize the muscles of the hips where the wide-spread abscess described by Larry Nassar's researchers is developed without a long-term review and also assesses any changes that are necessary to achieve the desired results.

rows.src: Mokgatlo wa Dijimnastiki wa USA le USOC di na le sepheo se tshwanang — e leng ho etsa hore papadi ya dijimnastiki, le tse ding, e bolokehe ka hohle ka moo ho ka kgonehang hore baatlelete ba latele ditoro tsa bona tikolohong e bolokehileng, e molemo mme e matlafaditsweng.
rows.ref: USA Gymnastics and the USOC have the same goal — making the sport of gymnastics, and others, as safe as possible for athletes to follow their dreams in a safe, positive and empowered environment.
rows.hyp: The USA Gymnastics Association and the USOC share a common goal — to make gymnastics, and other sports, as safe as possible for athletes to pursue their goals in a safe, healthy, and enriching environment.

rows.src: Nakong ya dikgetho tsa 1976 o eleditse Carter ho leano la tsa matjhabeng, mme a sebetsa e le Moeletsi wa Naha ho tsa Tshireletso (National Security Advisor (NSA)) ho tloha ka 1977 ho fihla ka 1981, a hlahlama Henry Kissinger.
rows.ref: During the 1976 selections he advised Carter on foreign policy, then served as National Security Advisor (NSA) from 1977 to 1981, succeeding Henry Kissinger.

rows.ref: As NSA, he assisted Carter in diplomatically handling world affairs, such as the Camp David Accords, 1978; normalizing US–China relations thought the late 1970s; the Iranian Revolution, which led to the Iran hostage crisis, 1979; and the Soviet invasion in Afghanistan, 1979.

rows.src: Mofuta wa pele wa tsela ya ho tsamaya o tsejwang ke ho tsamaya ka maoto, batho ba qadile ho tsamaya ba otlolohile dilemong tse dimillione tse pedi tse fetileng ha ho hlahella Homo Erectus (e bolelang monna ya otlolohileng).
